results.title: A Meta-analysis of Heart Rate Variability (HRV) and Psychopathology: An Investig
results.reason: This meta-analysis examines the relationship between heart rate variability (HRV) and psychopathology using the Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP) framework, which has direct clinical relevance for understanding physiological markers of mental health disorders across diagnostic categories.
results.authors: Tam Pham; Carly Johnco; Ana Neves; Wilson Lim Peng Hian; Heng Jiamin Gladys; Rachel Ygnacio; Miriam K. Forbes

results.title: Empirically derived phenotypes can reduce diagnostic heterogeneity
results.reason: The paper directly addresses diagnostic heterogeneity in mental health disorders, which has significant implications for clinical practice, assessment, and treatment planning. It focuses on internalizing disorders commonly encountered in clinical settings and offers empirical approaches to reduce heterogeneity through data-driven phenotyping.
results.authors: Miriam K. Forbes; John F. Buss; Daniel P. Moriarity; Eiko I. Fried; Holly Frances Levin-Aspenson; Lorenzo Lorenzo-Luaces; Kasey Stanton; Ashley L. Watts; Gregory W. Forbes

results.reason: This study evaluates large language models against psychotherapist qualification standards, which has direct clinical relevance for mental healthcare professionals and the potential integration of AI in clinical practice.

results.title: Dysphagia and Dysphonia in Parkinson’s Disease: Pathophysiological Mechanisms, T
results.reason: This paper directly addresses clinical psychology practice relevance by examining dysphagia and dysphonia in Parkinson's Disease, which are significant mental health and quality of life issues affecting a large proportion of patients. The paper covers assessment, diagnosis, and treatment approaches, making it highly relevant for practicing psychologists, speech therapists, and neurologists working with PD patients.
